integrity: In a cocktail party graph every vertex has one nonneighbor, so every zero set of size at least two is dominating and maximality forces at most one zero. A zero-free double Roman function of weight at most 2n+1 would have only one label-two defender, whose partner is an undefended label-one vertex. With one zero, defense costs exactly two units above the positive baseline, giving the lower bound 2n+1. Equality cannot use one label three because its partner would be an undefended label-one vertex; hence exactly two label-two vertices occur, both outside the zero vertex partner pair. This also yields the exact count.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats cocktail party graphs, equivalently complete multipartite graphs with every part of size two, and not arbitrary complete multipartite graphs.
Finite exhaustive verification covers n from two through five and is corroborative only.
The later arXiv copy of the foundational article was used for full-text inspection; the earliest verified public source date is taken from the repository record.
A differently phrased or non-indexed cocktail-party treatment may exist.
title: Maximal double Roman domination of cocktail party graphs
